newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty fraction below resistance, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty fraction below resistance, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty again edged closed toward strong resistance and likely intervention levels at 2.5 percent from the parity rate in early Tuesday trade as foreign investors paid for T-bills bought at Monday's tender.
Dealers said the market was carefull not to break upside resistance, wary of more central bank interventions after the bank bought currencies four out of five days last week.

"Right now the market is trying not to set off an intervention and it may absorb excess liquidity coming from foreign investor entry into Polish bills," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
At 0805 GMT the zloty was at 2.52/2.50 percent from the parity rate after opening at 2.57/2.48 and Monday's close at 2.52/2.47 percent.
It was at 3.1485/90 to the dollar against opening's 3.1485/00 and at 1.8511/15 to the mark against 1.8490/15.
At Monday's T-bill tender foreigners bought an estimated $50 million worth of Polish papers, much of which could go through the forex market on Tuesday, dealers said.
On the money market one-day deposits remained flat around 22.5 percent in early trade and dealers expected rates to hover around present levels for most of this week.

"No large changes can be expected in short-term rates until Thursday or Friday, when one-day cash could slip slightly from its present 22.40/22.70 percent band," said Krzysztof Poznanski, dealer at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA.
At 0820 GMT overnight rates were at 22.40/22.68 percent, flat from opening's 22.40/22.65 percent at 0630 GMT.
Tomorrow/next were at 22.51/22.79 percent agaisnt opening's 22.60/22.80 percent.
